tmp:3166: na'asin ben chorin ve-yotz'in min ha-galut — the state of becoming a free person and exiting exile, attained through joy which is the world of freedom
tmp:3167: olam ha-cherut — 'the world of freedom,' the kabbalistic realm (Binah/liberation) identified with joy, which enables one to direct the mind at will
tmp:3169: ve-yukhal le-yashev da'ato — the resulting capacity to settle one's mind (yishuv ha-da'at), achieved via joy governing the brain
tmp:3170: be-vadai yashuv el HaShem — the certain outcome of returning to God once one settles the mind on the purpose of all worldly desires
tmp:3171: sichah — prayer designated as 'conversation,' linked to siach ha-sadeh (Gen 2), the field-plants that join and empower one's prayer
tmp:3172: praying in the field — the practice whereby all the grasses enter into and strengthen one's prayer (basis of hitbodedut outdoors)
tmp:3177: sustaining oneself from the vitality of holiness — drawing life from the hidden divine life-force even in impure places (e.g., the great city of Rome)
tmp:3178: Torah itself — the Torah as an entity that walks before a person on his path ('when you walk it shall lead you,' Prov 6:22)
tmp:3179: the doubts and confusions preceding chiddushim — the state of uncertainty and mental turmoil that precedes every Torah innovation
tmp:3181: seh la-olah — the lamb for the burnt offering (olah), the korban that atones for sinful thoughts/musings of the heart
tmp:3182: returning and ascending to the Supernal Glory — the ascent effected when one asks 'Ayeh — where is the place of His Glory?' after falling into filthy places
tmp:3183: 'he will surely never stumble' — the guaranteed protection from error attained by walking in simplicity (temimut) rather than following one's own cleverness
tmp:3185: 'abirei lev ha-rechokim mi-tzedakah' (Isa 46:12) — the 'stout-hearted far from charity,' the hard stone-heart of those who withhold tzedakah
tmp:3186: lev even — the 'heart of stone' (Ezek 36:26), the hardened heart that tzedakah/water transforms (rock turned into a pool of water)
tmp:3187: YaBoK (yud-bet-kuf) — acronym Yichud-Berakhah-Kedushah (Unity, Blessing, Holiness), the river Yabbok as kabbalistic cipher formed through charity
tmp:3189: torei — the ox (Aramaic 'tora') of Shabbat 77b with its long tail, symbol of the great tzaddik to whom the false-prophet 'tail' attaches
tmp:3190: tzaddikim ha-gedolim — the great (publicly wondrous) tzaddikim, whose greatness gives the lying imposters a point of attachment
tmp:3191: navi u-moreh sheker — the false prophet and lying teacher (Isa 9:14), identified as 'the tail' attached to the great tzaddikim
tmp:3192: zanav — the tail (Isa 9:14), body-part symbol of the false prophet/hypocrite trailing after the great tzaddik (the long-tailed ox)
tmp:3193: gamla — the camel (Shabbat 77b, short-tailed), symbol of the simple tzaddik ('like a weaned child,' ke-gamul, Ps 131:1) who serves in silence
tmp:3194: tzaddik ha-pashut — the simple/plain tzaddik who acts with simplicity and silence, not speaking great and wondrous things
tmp:3196: the true tzaddik being saved from the flaw of the wicked donors' charity — protection from the blemish in tzedakah given by resha'im, effected via the imitators
tmp:3197: YaBoK in holiness — the holy configuration of Yichud-Berakhah-Kedushah produced when charity reaches the true tzaddik
tmp:3198: YaBoK as acronym — Yichud (unity), Berakhah (blessing), Kedushah (holiness), three aspects all stated of water/tzedakah
tmp:3199: the holy mouth of the tzaddik — the tzaddik's faculty of holy speech, received from charity-givers ('nidvot pi,' Ps 119:108)
tmp:3200: agam mayim — the 'pool of water' (Ps 114:8) into which the rock-heart is turned; water as symbol of tzedakah
tmp:3201: lev rakh — the soft/tender heart, the generous heart melted like water, opposite of the stone heart, source of tzedakah
tmp:3202: nedivei lev — the 'generous of heart' (freewill donors), from whom the tzaddik receives the speech of his mouth
tmp:3203: ba'alei tzedakah — givers of charity, the donors who supply the true tzaddik's holy speech
tmp:3204: seeing the King in His crown — beholding the King in beauty and greatness ('a king in his beauty your eyes shall behold,' Isa 33:17), not in smallness
tmp:3207: the joining of the imrei shefer with the King — the union of the 'beautiful words' (blessings/prayers from food) with the King, forming His crown
tmp:3208: chatunah — the wedding day ('on the day of his wedding,' Song 3:11), the day of the crown/union of King Solomon, symbol of the joining above
tmp:3209: ketoret — the incense offering, kabbalistically the aspect of berurim (refinements/sifting of sparks) from food
tmp:3210: ma'adanei melekh — 'royal delicacies' (Gen 49:20), the refined food from which imrei shefer (blessings) and the King's crown are made
tmp:3211: the essence of the honor and greatness of kingship — malkhut's true glory, achieved specifically through humility ('before honor, humility,' Prov 15:33)
tmp:3212: ikkar ha-malkhut — the essence of kingship itself, established through anavah (humility)
tmp:3213: that all Israel's livelihood must be received via the King — parnassah channeled through malkhut (the tree with 'food for all,' Dan 4:17)
tmp:3214: a person doing good — the good deeds a person performs, which God regards while overlooking the bad ('He beheld no iniquity in Jacob,' Num 23:21)
tmp:3215: God guiding him with hashgachah — divine providence directing the person as a result of judging favorably/looking only at the good
tmp:3216: on Shabbat through joy — the Shabbat state in which simchah frees one from weekday servitude, making Da'at whole and fear of God complete
